description:
V1.1.0
Major update, adding 18 aviation calculators
Ui remake and fixing bugs

MetarNow is a firmware for the Cardputer focused on aviation use. It gives fast access to METAR, TAF, airport info, alerts, decoded weather, and 18 aviation calculators, in a simple handheld UI designed for the tiny screen.
Setup is straightforward:
On first boot it walks you through sound on/off, Wi-Fi setup, and choosing a home station, controls. After that, you can instantly open your home airport by clicking ENTER or search for any other station.
Core usage:
-Open your home weather instantly
-Search another airport when needed
-Use TAB to cycle through views (METAR → TAF → alerts → detailed weather → airport info)
-Press R anytime to refresh data
Extra controls & shortcuts:
-On the search screen:
-ENTER with no input → goes to your saved home station
-FN + W → scan for Wi-Fi networks
-FN + S → open Settings

Calculators control:
Up/Down fields, Enter next/open, Tab modes, G graph where available

Back deletes input first, then returns when the field is empty
In Wi-Fi scan:
-R → rescan networks
Wi-Fi behavior:
-Automatically connects to saved network if available
Otherwise opens scan so you can connect to a new one
Settings let you manage:
-brightness, saved Wi-Fi, sound, and controls.

V1.1.0
Added a new icon-based main menu:

WX DATA | CALCULATOR | SETTINGS

Also improved scrolling animations and fixed saved WiFi behavior, so known networks connect again without asking for the password every time.
skip connecting to a wifi for offline use.

New Calculator section

This was inspired by feedback/ideas from my previous post. The new calculator section now includes 18 aviation calculators:

WCA / GS calculates wind correction angle, heading, ground speed, drift, and leg time. Includes graph view.
XWIND calculates runway headwind/tailwind and crosswind components. Includes graph view.

ck error/opening angle and closing correction.

Overview:
This is a shared program for both robot units and controllers. Double-clicking the A button switches between modes.
Supported M5 Devices:
• 	M5AtomS3 series
• 	M5Capsule
Compatible Accessories:
In addition to the supported M5 devices above, the following accessories (or equivalents with matching pin layouts) are assumed:
• 	5-servo connection board for M5Capsule
https://www.switch-science.com/products/9475
• 	4-servo connection board for M5ATOM
https://www.switch-science.com/products/9474
• 	Compact joystick controller board for M5ATOM S3 (board only)
https://www.switch-science.com/products/9522
Operation:
• 	[Robot Mode] While holding the A button, servos move (for operation check).
• 	[Controller Mode] Pressing the A button retrieves the battery level of a nearby robot.
※ Only effective for models with built-in batteries; not supported on Atom series.
• 	Double-clicking the A button cycles through modes for robot and controller use:
Left-hand controller → Right-hand controller → UGOKUPad → ESP-NOW (robot mode) → loop
• 	[Controller Mode] Long-pressing the A button registers a nearby powered-on robot.
※ If no robot is registered, commands are broadcast to all robots simultaneously.

name: Multi-Tools ADV (Timer, Dados e Sorteio)
description:
O Multi-Tools ADV é o verdadeiro "canivete suíço" para o seu M5Cardputer. Desenvolvido para ser um utilitário de bolso diário, este aplicativo reúne quatro ferramentas essenciais em uma única interface limpa e direta. Ele é o companheiro perfeito para sessões de estudo focadas (técnica Pomodoro), medição de tempo em tarefas e, principalmente, para noites de jogos de tabuleiro com os amigos.

Seja substituindo dados perdidos de um jogo de RPG, sorteando letras para uma partida de "Stop/Adedanha" ou cravando o tempo de uma apresentação, este aplicativo elimina a necessidade de pegar o celular e se distrair com notificações.

Como Funciona a Dinâmica (Os 4 Módulos)

    Timer de Foco (Ajustável com Memória): Muito mais que um simples contador regressivo. Você ajusta o tempo exato que precisa direto no teclado. O grande diferencial é a Memória de Ciclo: se você configurar para 1 minuto (ou 25 minutos para um Pomodoro), quando o tempo acabar e o alarme tocar, basta apertar "Reset" e ele volta instantaneamente para a sua configuração personalizada, pronto para o próximo round sem precisar ajustar tudo de novo.

    Cronômetro de Precisão: Um medidor de tempo progressivo clássico. Ele exibe minutos, segundos e milissegundos, perfeito para registrar recordes de tempo de leitura, montagem de projetos ou atividades físicas.

    Rolar Dados (D6): Esqueceu os dados do jogo de tabuleiro? Este módulo gera rolagens 100% aleatórias. Você pode escolher rolar apenas 1 dado, 2 dados ou 3 dados simultaneamente na tela com o toque de um botão.

    Sorteio de Letras: Um gerador automático que puxa uma letra aleatória do alfabeto (A a Z) a cada aperto de botão. Indispensável para jogos de palavras clássicos em grupo.

Mapeamento de Controles e Atalhos

Menu Principal:

    Teclas 1, 2, 3 ou 4: Acessam os respectivos módulos.

    Tecla 0: Retorna ao Menu Principal de qualquer lugar do aplicativo.

name: NES Emulator
description:
I just fetched this from the internet

You need an SD card with .nes files on it. That's probably all what you need.

NES Emulator for M5Stack Tab5 with File Browser
NES emulator for M5Stack Tab5 with built-in file browser for selecting ROM files.

Features
File Browser: Browse and select NES ROM files from SD card
USB Host Support: Use USB gamepad (PS5 DualSense only) for navigation
I2C Input Support: Joystick2, Scroll buttons, CardKeyBoard
Display: 1280×720 landscape orientation
Audio: ES8388 codec support
Hardware Requirements
M5Stack Tab5 (ESP32-P4)
SD Card (FAT32) with ROM files in /sd/roms/ folder
USB gamepad (optional, for navigation)
ROM Files
Place your .nes ROM files in /sd/roms/ folder on the SD card.

Example:

/sd/roms/
  ├── super_mario.nes
  ├── zelda.nes
  └── metroid.nes
Building
cd nes_tab5_usb_host
export IDF_PATH=/path/to/esp-idf
source $IDF_PATH/export.sh
idf.py build
Flashing
Option 1: Flash from Source (Recommended)
cd nes_tab5_usb_host
export IDF_PATH=/path/to/esp-idf
source $IDF_PATH/export.sh
idf.py -p /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX flash
Option 2: Flash from GitHub Release
Download all three files from the release:

bootloader.bin
partition-table.bin
nes_tab5_file_browser.bin
Then flash them using esptool:

# Make sure ESP-IDF environment is loaded
export IDF_PATH=/path/to/esp-idf
source $IDF_PATH/export.sh

# Flash all three files
esptool --chip esp32p4 --port /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX --baud 921600 write_flash \
  0x0 bootloader.bin \
  0x8000 partition-table.bin \
  0x10000 nes_tab5_file_browser.bin
Important: All three files are required! Flashing only the main binary will result in "invalid header" errors.

Usage
Insert SD card with ROM files in /sd/roms/ folder
Connect USB gamepad (optional)
Power on Tab5
File browser will appear showing available ROM files
Navigate with D-Pad Up/Down
Press Start or A to launch selected game
To return to file browser, restart Tab5
Controls
File Browser
D-Pad Up/Down: Navigate file list
Start or A: Launch selected game
In-Game (PS5 DualSense)
Cross (PS5): NES B
Circle (PS5): NES A
Square: Turbo B
Triangle: Turbo A
Create: Select
Options: Start
D-Pad / Left Stick: D-Pad
Project Structure
nes_tab5_usb_host/
├── main/
│   └── app_main.cpp          # Main application with file browser
├── components/
│   ├── m5stack_tab5/         # BSP for Tab5
│   └── nes_emulator/         # NES emulator (nofrendo)
│       ├── include/
│       │   └── nes_osd.h     # OSD functions
│       └── src/
│           └── nes_osd.c     # OSD implementation
├── CMakeLists.txt
├── sdkconfig.defaults
└── partitions.csv

name: NNOs - NoName Operating System
description:
**Updated**
Added usb audio support (fn + o modal) / Barely tested, needs a powered hub afaik.

Significant rework:
- Runs on hybrid arduino3/espidf
- New logging system wired to fn + d, configured via fn+g
- SndRec32 can open pls file exclusively containing web radios links (mp3, 128kbps only), display a menu and hopefully play them correctly
- ImageViewer received png and jpg performance enhancement and bugfix
- DosEdit is more stable and capable
- Added Micropython (with capability to run .py files you would have created with DosEdit for example) and a REPL. Super experimental though.
- Added a MicroCLI to run some orphaned commands not found in apps
- Greatly enhanced IRCamera app for Thermal module (mlx90640)
- CardKB2 and ble keyboard support via dedicated apps
- STOrk app (mimic a stork toy that distord voice) buggy app nonetheless
- Latest Ardugurl BUT without IRAM_ATTR so lower performance than standalone (by design)
- few more modals, driver improvements etc... 

A snappy, all-in-one OS suite packing 20+ apps for your Cardputer!
Play Ardugurl and Chip8, or use DosEdit, SndRec32, Canary, and a REPL Calc.
Features advanced keyboard modes and global Fn-shortcuts.
Full disclosure: rushed release! Expect bugs, crashes, and weird UI quirks :) (use Esc, left arrow, del or reset if stuck !)
SD card heavily required. Download it, break it, and kindly report the bugs!

Acknowledgments:
Massive thanks to the developers of the libraries that make this possible (among others): M5Unified & M5Cardputer, ggwave (for data over sound), minimp3 (by lieff), JPEGDEC/PNGdec (by bitbank2), FastLED, and NimBLE-Arduino.

TL;DR:
NNOs (NoName Operating System) is a fast, all-in-one suite that turns your Cardputer into a proper pocket Swiss Army knife. I got tired of flashing different apps every time I needed a specific tool, so I packed over 20 of them into one highly responsive build.

I rushed this release (feel free to ask why). The experience isn't fully unified yet, the UI might jump around a bit depending on the app, and there are absolutely some crashes hiding in there. I still have to debug and polish things, but it's surprisingly usable. Don't depend on it for life-support, and kindly report bugs!
⌨️ Advanced Keyboard Modes & Global Shortcuts

Because diving into menus is slow, I've hardcoded global shortcuts and custom keyboard layers directly into the driver. You can use these anywhere in the OS.

Global Fn-Shortcuts (Hold Fn + Key):

    w: WiFi Modal

    z: BLE Modal

    y: Battery Modal

    k: Clock Modal

    l: LED Modal

    u: USB Modal

    j: Joystick Modal

    b: GPIO Button Modal

    d: Diagnostic Modal

    c: Cycle Display

    s: Silent Screenshot (Saves directly to SD)

    - / =: Volume Down / Volume Up

Hardware Sleep:

    G0 Button (Side): Press at any time to drop into instant light-sleep and save battery. Press any key to wake back up instantly.

Keyboard Modes (Tap modifiers to lock layers):

    Caps Lock: Double-tap Shift

    Fn Lock: Double-tap Fn

    Sticky Fn: Single-tap Opt. The very next key you press will use the Fn layer, then it auto-reverts to normal.

    Strict Navigation: Double-tap Alt. Maps the right-side symbol keys (;, ., ,, /) into a one-handed directional pad.


🛠️ App Survival Guide

Since some of these apps have custom controls, here is a quick guide on how to actually use them:

Cardputer Canary (Network Monitor)
A powerful uptime and status monitor. It loads a CSV file from your SD card. Your CSV needs at least an Alias and a Target, but can also specify Type (PING, HTTP, HTTPS, DNS), Payload, Headers, and Interval.

    Press m to toggle between the dense Matrix view and the detailed List view.

    Shows active UP/DOWN/WARN status and ping response times.
Example file:
Alias,Target,Type,Payload,Headers,Interval
ROUTER,192.168.1.1,PING,,,60
GOOGLE,google.com,PING,,,300
MY-SITE,example.com,HTTP,Example Domain,User-Agent:Cardputer/1.0,300
DNS-TEST,one.one.one.one,DNS,1.0.0.1,,60
BAD-URL,nonexistent.test,HTTP,,,60
HIGH-LAT,8.8.8.8,PING,,,5

SndRec32 (WinAudio)
A classic sound recorder.

    Use keys 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 to activate the top UI buttons (Seek Back, Seek Fwd, Play/Pause, Stop, Record).

    Press l to load a new file.

    It records 16-bit 8000Hz WAVs to a folder called sd:/Esprec32/. Stop playback to be able to record. It also plays MP3s.

REPL Calculator
A Read-Eval-Print-Loop calculator. Type an expression and press Enter.

    Supports variables (x = 5 + pi), hex conversions (toHex(255)), and math functions (sin(), sqrt(), f2c()).

    Holds your last result in the variable ans.

    Type help to see all available commands.

DosEdit
A text editor paying tribute to the MS-DOS days. Type your text normally.

    Press the MENU (or ESC) key to jump focus to the top menu bar where you can Save, Open, or Copy/Paste lines.

    Use arrow keys to navigate the dropdowns.

Icon Editor
Pixel art on the go.

    Use the arrow keys to move the cursor, and Enter to toggle pixels.

    Hit the MENU key to open the options to Save/Load BMPs, or export your drawing directly into a C++ byte array in sd:/icons/icon_code.txt.

Carlendar
An offline calendar viewer. Put a calendar.ics file on your SD root and let it parse the events.

    Use [ and ] to navigate backward and forward between months or days.

    Press t to jump back to today.

    Press j to jump to a specific date (YYYY-MM-DD), or s to text-search your events.

Image Viewer
Open a .jpg, .png, or .bmp via the file selector.

    Once the image is open, use the Left and Right arrow keys to instantly cycle through all other images in that same folder.

    Press Up to open the file selector again.

IR Camera
(Requires the MLX90640 unit).

    Press Enter to cycle through the temperature scales (Human, Fridge, Full range).

    Press Right (Forward) to toggle fullscreen mode.

name: NTRIP Client for M5Stack StickC Plus2
description: The program is an NTRIP client for the M5StickC Plus2 written in MicroPython. It connects to Wi-Fi and then to an NTRIP server to download RTCM correction data, which it forwards via UART to a GNSS receiver. It reads NMEA messages (GGA, GST), determines position, altitude, fix status (GPS, DGPS, FLOAT, RTK), and the number of satellites in use. It calculates the age of RTCM corrections and displays it as a progress bar. The screen shows coordinates, dE/dN deviations, timers for different fix modes, and Wi-Fi and NTRIP status. It includes automatic reconnect logic, timeouts, authentication error blocking, and sound alerts for key status changes.

A deliberately simple app — I built it after running into charging
problems on my Nesso N1, so if you hit the same, it might help.

More on GitHub: https://github.com/MateuszParol/NessoCharger

name: Nesso_base
description:
Arduino firmware for the **Arduino Nesso N1** handheld controller — a
WiFi/BLE/LoRa-enabled base station that controls a remote robot platform over a
selectable wireless link: WiFi-UDP, TCP, BLE, or LoRa (CRC-checked NessoLink
RemoteFrame protocol with receiver failsafe). Features a 240×135px TFT display
with a multi-mode menu, battery monitoring, 1–3 joystick input (Adafruit seesaw
gamepad, M5Stack Mini JoyC HAT, and/or M5Stack Unit JoyStick2 — one drive stick
plus up to two aux sticks, with per-stick orientation adaptation, calibration,
and deadzone settings), IR and 433 MHz RF remote control, RFID card scanning,
Speaker Hat 2 (MAX98357A) audio, an experimental BLE HID gamepad mode, and a
web-based file manager.

Robot side: control frames are encoded by the **NessoLink** Arduino library —
install it from the IDE Library Manager (or `arduino-cli lib install NessoLink`,
source: github.com/ugursayar/NessoLink) and decode with `nessoDecode()`. The
library ships ready-made receiver examples for ESP32 (`RobotReceiverUDP/TCP/BLE`),
Arduino Uno R4 WiFi (`UnoR4ReceiverUDP/TCP/BLE`), and M5 Cardputer ADV + Cap
LoRa 1262 (`CardputerAdvLoRaReceiver`), so a robot can be up and driving with a
few lines around `applyMotors()`.

## What's new in v1.1.0

- Selectable robot TX link: WiFi-UDP / TCP / BLE / LoRa (NessoLink RemoteFrame v1/v2)
- Up to three joysticks at once — seesaw gamepad, Mini JoyC HAT, Unit JoyStick2:
  one drive + two aux sticks, per-stick rotation adaptation, selectable primary
- Controller settings screen: calibration, deadzone, axis swap/invert, TX link,
  stick mount, primary stick
- Speaker Hat 2 (MAX98357A) audio support
- Experimental BLE HID gamepad mode (off by default)
- Smoother drive mixer and non-blocking TCP reconnects; button-read and boot
  robustness fixes

    Improved BLE Spam
    Deauth: fixed 5GHz HT40 tuning, added burst loops, and removed rate limiting
    Reorganized settings menu into more categories
    Directly iterate to channels when deauthing multiple APs
    Optimised wardriving dwell times, added active probing and improved validation
    Wardriving now builds role-aware channel plans for split capture (primary 5 GHz, helper 2.4 GHz when both are available)
    Wardriving heartbeat now reports helper merge stats (helper=merged/received) for link visibility
    Reworked wardriving Wi-Fi dedupe into peek/commit flow to avoid consuming dedupe state before a successful CSV write
    Shortened delays for misc display menu building for more responsive feel
    Improved clock view responsiveness
    Increased BadUSB VSense delay to improve reliability of USB enumeration
    Improved CLI scan validation and status messaging for invalid durations and failed timed scans
    Improved CLI sd read/write/append reliability checks to report short writes and stream errors
    Improved task startup error handling for DIAL, Karma, Deauth, Beacon, EAPOL, DHCP Starvation, and SAE Flood
    Improved BLE capture startup flow to fail fast when handler registration or scan start fails
    Optimized PineAP detection memory model by lazily allocating detection tables at start and freeing them on stop
    Reworked PineAP detection logging to use a single queued worker task instead of per-detection task creation
    Reworked PCAP writer buffering to use a fixed static packet slot pool instead of per-packet heap allocations
    Reduced splash screen hold time from 2000ms to 900ms
    Refactored surface colors to be consistent across the UI
    Changed default screen timeout to 30s
    Miscellaneous fixes, improvements and refactors
    Fixed feberis pro spelling

    Fixed station deauth channel lookup
    Fixed potential NULL dereference in command registration when strdup fails under low memory
    Fixed silent serial startup failures by validating queue and task creation in serial_manager_init
    Fixed race-prone stop behavior in SAE flood by waiting for task exit before freeing crypto context
    Fixed race-prone restart behavior in Karma and Beacon by waiting/cleaning lingering tasks on stop
    Fixed DHCP starvation reporting success while socket/send operations were failing
    Fixed select CLI parse errors that omitted the invalid token and improved index list boundary checks
    Fixed GPS latitude parsing for GLL sentences (was using 3-digit degree width instead of 2)
    Fixed BLE not initializing when selecting a flipper
    Fixed crash when deinitializing BLE
    Fixed BLE stop hangs by draining active scan callbacks before shutdown and reducing heavy callback work
    Potentially fixed "Connect to saved WiFi" resets on repeated use
    Fixed GPS satellites logic
    Fixed misc wardriving issues
    Fixed wardriving AP loss where entries seen before a valid GPS fix could be skipped later by premature dedupe mutation
    Fixed 5GHz deauthing

    Fixed crash starting karma attack

    Fixed joystick and touch input not checking if display is dimmed

name: Old Time Radio Player Live Internet Radio Retro Stream
description:
WiFi Internet Radio for the M5Stack Core1 Basic — a port of the excellent winRadio project by Volos Projects, re-skinned with a custom retro old-time radio aesthetic. 📻

Sound is not great. It is Old Time Radio, all of them have been converted from records, to reels, to tapes to probably multiple digital formats, over the last 80 years or so. Some shows may sound very poor. I recommend switching stations until a better sounding show comes on. 8 stations to choose from. 
Features
WiFi internet radio streaming 
Retro old-time radio UI skin
8 preset stations (ROKiT Radio Network classic/OTR streams, 48 kbps MP3)
Scrolling song/metadata ticker
VU meter bar graph
Bass / Treble / Volume controls
WiFi credentials stored in NVS via captive portal setup
Hold BtnA during 3-second boot window to re-enter WiFi setup
Button Mapping
Button	Normal Mode	Sound Settings Mode
BtnA (left)	Open sound settings	Exit back to radio
BtnB (middle)	Cycle station	Select next parameter
BtnC (right)	Cycle volume	Increase selected parameter

When you boot the device a Captive Portal will open to set up your WiFi connection. ON your phone or PC. IF it fails to open, turn off your moblile data and browse to 192.168.4.1 in your mobile browser WHILE connected to the CORE. 

Credits
Original project: winRadio by Volos Projects
Original hardware target: Waveshare ESP32-S3 with ST7789 240×240 display.
All core audio streaming logic, station management, and UI concept by Volos Projects.

Ported and Modified by Coreymillia

name: OpenWiFi Scanner - Cardputer & ADV
description:
Works with both Cardputer models.

This tool continuously scans for open networks, searching for internet access, and generates a report of the surrounding Wi-Fi networks. It displays the detected networks, categorized by their security status.

SCREEN:
- Green: Indicates networks that provide open access to the internet.
- White: Indicates networks that are open without encryption but may not provide internet access.
- Orange: Indicates networks that use outdated or weak encryption, potentially at risk.
- Red: Indicates networks that are securely encrypted and protected.

LED:
- Green LED: Lights up when open networks or networks with web access are detected.
- Orange LED: Lights up when vulnerable networks are detected.
- Red LED: Lights up when only closed networks are found.

SPEAKER:
- One bip tone: Plays when a vulnerable network is detected.
- Two bip Tone: Plays when an open network is found.
- Melody tone: Plays when a web access network is available.


Disclaimer:

This tool is intended solely for educational and security purposes. It is designed to help users understand and assess the security of Wi-Fi networks. Do not use this tool to attempt unauthorized access to private networks. Unauthorized access to networks is illegal and unethical. Always obtain proper permission from the network owner before performing any scans or security assessments.

name: Oraculo
description:
O Oráculo Mágico transforma o seu M5Cardputer em um verdadeiro vidente de bolso! Inspirado no clássico brinquedo místico "Magic 8-Ball", este aplicativo é perfeito para ajudar a tomar daquelas decisões difíceis do dia a dia, prever o futuro ou simplesmente garantir boas risadas em uma roda de amigos.

O sistema conta com um gerador de aleatoriedade avançado (usando o ruído analógico do processador como "semente mística") para garantir que cada resposta seja única e imprevisível. Ele divide as respostas entre afirmações positivas, negativas e misteriosas, mantendo o suspense a cada consulta.

Como Funciona a Dinâmica
A interação com o Oráculo é simples, direta e envolta em mistério:

    A Concentração: O aplicativo exibe uma tela de espera mística. O usuário deve segurar o Cardputer, concentrar-se profundamente e fazer uma pergunta de "Sim ou Não" (mentalmente ou em voz alta).

    A Consulta: Ao pressionar o botão, o Oráculo entra em modo de transe. A tela exibe uma animação ou mensagem de "Consultando os astros..." para criar um breve suspense.

    A Revelação: O gerador de aleatoriedade escolhe uma das dezenas de respostas programadas (como "Sim, com certeza", "Minhas fontes dizem que não", ou "Nebuloso, tente de novo") e a exibe em destaque no centro da tela.

    Novo Ciclo: O Oráculo fica aguardando a próxima dúvida existencial do usuário.

Mapeamento de Controles e Atalhos

A interface foi desenhada para ser operada com um único dedo, mantendo o foco na brincadeira:

    Tecla ENTER ou Botão G0 (Botão lateral do M5Cardputer): Inicia a consulta aos astros e revela a resposta do Oráculo.

    Tecla ESC (ou DEL): Limpa a resposta atual e prepara a tela para a próxima pergunta.

name: PORKCHOP
description:
--[ The Pig in the Machine

      They said pwnagotchi was dead.
      They said the ESP32 couldn't do it.
      They were wrong about both.

      A piglet woke up inside your Cardputer.
      It learned to sniff the spectrum.
      It learned to hunt the handshakes.
      It learned to track the clients.

      And somewhere along the way... it started keeping score.

      50 ranks. 10 class tiers. 64 achievements. Buffs that stack.
      The more you hunt, the stronger it gets.
      The longer you walk, the more it remembers.
      Your crimes become experience points.

      This is not a tool. This is a companion.
      A pocket-sized accomplice with moods, opinions, and a temper.
      It judges your network choices. It mocks your signal strength.
      It celebrates when you capture. It sulks when you don't.
      It watches the weather. It counts your steps.
      It demands challenges. Three per session. No excuses.

      You don't use PORKCHOP.
      You raise it.

      And when they wipe your flash, when they nuke your NVS,
      when they think they've reset you to zero...

      The pig remembers.
      The pig always remembers.


  --[ What Lives Inside

      [*] OINK MODE - Active WiFi hunt. Channel hopping. Handshake capture.
          Automatic PMKID extraction. Surgical deauth. Disassoc on demand.

--[ 1 - WHAT THE HELL IS THIS

----[ 1.1 - THE ELEVATOR PITCH

    PORKCHOP runs on M5Cardputer (ESP32-S3, 240MHz, 8MB flash).
    it turns a pocket keyboard into a WiFi pentesting companion with:

    - dual-band (2.4 + 5GHz) packet capture via ESP32-C5 coprocessor
    - EAPOL handshake + PMKID extraction (hashcat 22000 + PCAP)
    - dual-band GPS wardriving with WiGLE v1.6 export

    - beacon injection with vendor IE fingerprinting
    - device-to-device sync via ESP-NOW (PigSync)
    - a personality system with opinions about your choices

    it's a learning tool for WiFi security research.
    the difference between tool and weapon is the hand holding it. 
    wink. wink.


----[ 1.2 - THE LINEUP (what you're getting into)

    words are cheap. pixels are evidence.

    THE PIG IN THE FLESH:

    ![PIG PEN](docs/images/porkchop.jpg)
    *the pigs. awake. judging. 240x135 pixels of unsolicited opinions.*

    THE HARDWARE NAKED:

    ![Cardputer ADV with CapLoRa module](docs/images/hardware_cardputer_adv.jpg)
    *cardputer ADV + CapLoRa868. GPS + LoRa on a keyboard.*
    *smaller than your phone. more opinions than your family.*

    ![The full kit - Cardputer + CapLoRa + GPS antenna](docs/images/hardware_full_kit.jpg)
    *the full loadout. everything the pig needs to judge your neighborhood.*

    (photos missing? we're working on it. the pig doesn't pose for free.
     the horse refused the photoshoot entirely. barn lighting was wrong.)


----[ 1.3 - HARDWARE SPECS

    M5Cardputer (M5Stack StampS3):
        (EAPOL has M1, M2, M3, M4. the hardware is M5.
         the fifth message. the one the protocol never sent.
         we are the frame after the handshake.)
        - ESP32-S3FN8: 240MHz dual-core, 512KB SRAM, 8MB flash
        - NO PSRAM (~300KB usable heap. every byte matters.)
        - 240x135 IPS LCD (ST7789V2)
        - QWERTY keyboard (56 keys)
        - SD card slot (FAT32, shared SPI bus with CapLoRa)
        - NeoPixel LED (GPIO 21)
        - USB-C (power + serial)

    Optional:
        - GPS module: AT6668/ATGM336H (Grove port G1/G2 or CapLoRa)
        - CapLoRa868 module (G15/G13 GPS, SX1262 LoRa shares SD SPI)
        - M5MonsterC5 (ESP32-C5 WiFi 6 dual-band coprocessor):
          Grove UART to Cardputer. runs JanOS/projectZero firmware.
          the pig's 5GHz ear. plugs in. speaks 802.11ax.
          optional onboard AT6668 GPS (forwarded over UART).
        - Cardputer ADV: BMI270 IMU enables dial mode in Spectrum
        - your legs, for wardriving. no judgment on wheels.

    GET THE HARDWARE (the part where we sell out):

        look. we're going to be transparent here.
        these are affiliate links. we get a cut.
        you get a pig. capitalism works (sometimes).

        the pig doesn't mass-produce itself.
        the pig needs a body. the body needs a store.
        the store needs a link. the link needs a click.
        you see where this is going.

        M5Stack Cardputer ADV (the pig's body):
        https://shop.m5stack.com/products/m5stack-cardputer-adv-version-esp32-s3/?ref=xqezhcga

        CapLoRa 1262 (GPS + LoRa module, the pig's sense of direction):
        https://shop.m5stack.com/products/cap-lora-1262-for-cardputer-adv-sx1262-atgm336h?ref=xqezhcga

        buying through these links funds:
        1. coffee (which becomes code)
        2. code (which becomes bugs)
        3. bugs (which become trauma)
        4. trauma (which becomes coffee)
        5. the circle continues. you're an investor now.

        not buying? also valid. the pig judges purchases,
        not people. clone it, build it, source it however.
        open source means open source.

        but if you DO click... the pig remembers its friends.


----[ 1.4 - ARCHITECTURE (for the silicon gourmets)

    THE CORE:
    cooperative main loop. porkchop.update() (SFX ticks inside),
    Display::update(), Mood::update(). the pig's vital organs.
    single PorkchopMode enum, 24 states. one mode lives. the others wait.
    the pig is a finite state machine with infinite opinions.
    the horse is a barn with load-bearing feelings.

    THE MEMORY WAR:
    no PSRAM means ~300KB internal SRAM for everything.
    TLS needs ~35KB contiguous (kMinContigForTls in heap_policy.h).
    WiFi driver init needs ~70KB (why preInitWiFiDriverEarly() exists).
    the heap fragments like your relationship with sleep.

    HEAP CONDITIONING:
    boot runs a 5-phase ritual: frag blocks (50x1KB), struct blocks
    (20x3KB), TLS test allocs (26KB, 32KB, 40KB). exploits ESP-IDF's
    TLSF allocator for O(1) coalescing. the result: a clean brain
    for TLS handshakes. percussive maintenance for memory.
    the horse calls this "barn defragmentation."
    the barn denies having a defragmentation problem.
    the barn is the horse. denial is structural.

    HEAP MONITORING:
    heap_health.h samples every 1s. auto-triggers conditioning when
    health drops below 65%, clears when it recovers above 75%.
    adaptive cooldown: 15-60s between rounds (scales with heap state).
    the heart bar at the bottom of the screen is heap health.
    100% = clean. 0% = swiss cheese. the pig's blood pressure, basically.

    THE EVENT BUS:
    max 32 queued events, 16 processed per update tick.
    MODE_CHANGE, ML_RESULT, GPS_FIX, GPS_LOST,
    HANDSHAKE_CAPTURED, NETWORK_FOUND, DEAUTH_SENT,
    ROGUE_AP_DETECTED, OTA_AVAILABLE, LOW_BATTERY.
    the pig processes feelings through a state machine.
    the horse processes feelings through a k-hole.

    DUAL-CORE PATTERN:
    WiFi promiscuous callbacks run on core 1 (WiFi task).
    they CANNOT allocate memory or call Serial. instead:
    callback sets volatile flags + writes to static pools.
    main loop on core 0 checks flags and processes safely.
    this is the deferred event pattern. it keeps the WDT happy.
    WDT = Watchdog Timer. also What Did (The pig) Think.

    STATIC POOLS:
    OINK pre-allocates PendingHandshakeFrame pendingHsPool[4]
    (~13KB in BSS). permanent. std::atomic indices for lock-free
    producer/consumer between WiFi task and main loop.
    the pig pays rent on memory it might never use.

    NetworkRecon:
    shared background scanning service. OINK, DONOHAM, SPECTRUM,
    and WARHOG all consume the same getNetworks() vector.
    spinlock mutex with RAII CriticalSection wrapper.
    channel hop order: 1, 6, 11, then 2-5, 7-10, 12-13.
    max 200 networks tracked. the pig has limits.
    (200 is generous. the heap disagrees.)

    JANUS HOG (ESP32-C5 COPROCESSOR):
    the pig grew a second ear. the 5GHz one.
    M5MonsterC5 board connected via Grove UART (115200 8N1).
    runs JanOS/projectZero firmware. speaks scan, attack, monitor.
    peripheral service like GPS -- runs every loop iteration,
    zero heap allocations, all static BSS (~7KB total).
    double-buffered scan cache (64 entries x2) prevents UI flicker.
    5GHz networks injected into NetworkRecon transparently.
    modes don't care WHERE the data came from. they just eat.
    GPS forwarding from C5's onboard AT6668 when local GPS sleeps.
    handshake file import via base64 framed transfer with CRC32.
    the pig doesn't scan 5GHz. the pig DELEGATES 5GHz.
    management is a skill. the pig has management skills now.
    the horse would delegate too but the barn has no peripherals.

    BOOT GUARD:
    RTC memory tracks rapid reboots. 3 in 60 seconds = force IDLE.
    crash loops get the nuclear option. the pig learns from pain.
    the horse calls this progress.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

--[ 2 - MODES (what the pig does)

    one keypress from IDLE. zero menus. zero friction.
    each mode changes the pig's vocabulary.
    this is not a bug. this is character development.


----[ 2.1 - OINK MODE (active hunt) [O]

    the pig goes rowdy. opinions about APs become actionable.
    snout to the wire. tusks out. both bands.

    CAPABILITIES:
        - dual-band hunting (2.4GHz local + 5GHz via JanusHog C5)
        - 7-state auto-attack state machine:
            SCANNING    = 5s network enumeration
            PMKID_HUNT  = clientless probe sweep (10-30s adaptive)
            NEXT_TARGET = composite scoring selects next victim
            LOCKING     = channel hold, client discovery
            ATTACKING   = 2-phase deauth (knock burst + maintenance drip)
            WAITING     = 4.5s listen for M3/M4 after M1
            BORED       = 30s cooldown when no targets available
        - promiscuous mode 802.11 frame capture (2.4GHz)
        - EAPOL handshake extraction (M1-M4, validates sequence)
        - PMKID hunting: clientless attack sweep across all APs.
          auth + assoc per IEEE spec. 300ms timeout per AP.
          64-bit bitset tracks probed networks. no re-probes.
          (the AP just volunteers its PMKID. trust issues are real.)
        - 5GHz background attacks: C5 coprocessor handles targets
          on channels 36-165 in parallel. fire-and-forget dispatch.
          45s timeout per target. the pig hunts two bands at once.
        - deauth (Reason 7) + disassoc (Reason 8):
          2-phase burst: knock (2 frames <3ms) + drip (1 frame/250ms)
          bidirectional: AP->client AND client->AP
          auto-pause on M1 observed (let the handshake happen)
        - PMF detection: Protected Management Frames networks
          get marked immune. the pig respects armor.

        1. create /m5porkchop/wpa-sec/wpasec_key.txt
        2. contents: 32-char hex key from wpa-sec.stanev.org
        3. key file auto-deletes after import

    FEATURES:
        - upload .22000 and .pcap captures
        - download potfile (cracked results)
        - per-capture crack status indicators
        - ALREADY UPLOADED tracking (no phantom submissions)
        - XP award for submissions

    press [S] in LOOT > HASHES to sync.


----[ 5.3 - IF UPLOADS FAIL

    TLS needs ~35KB contiguous heap.

    1. stop promiscuous mode (exit OINK/DNH)
    2. check DIAGNOSTICS for heap status
    3. let heap_health auto-condition (wait 30s)
    4. try again

    HeapGates::checkTlsGates() runs before every upload.
    if it says no, the pig can't negotiate TLS.
    the pig tried. the heap said no. the pig respects boundaries.
    (the heap does not respect your schedule. ESP32 gonna ESP32.)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

--[ 6 - PIGSYNC (son of a pig)

    ESP-NOW encrypted sync between POPS (Porkchop) and
    SON (s3rloin). the prodigal son answers the phone.


----[ 6.1 - THE PROTOCOL

    press [2] from IDLE to enter PigSync.

    DISCOVERY: broadcast on channel 1. s3rloin responds
    with MAC, pending capture count, flags, RSSI.

    CONNECTION: CMD_HELLO -> RSP_HELLO (session token +
    data channel assignment). channels 3/4/8/9/13 selected
    to avoid congested 1/6/11.

    DATA TRANSFER: chunked, 238 bytes per fragment.
    sequence numbers, CRC32 verification, ACK per chunk.
    5 retries per chunk. 60 second transfer timeout.

    ENCRYPTION: ESP-NOW encrypted unicast.
    PMK and LMK are hardcoded in pigsync_protocol.h.
    (both sides must match. source is truth.
     yes, the keys are pig-themed. obviously.)

    BOUNTIES: wardriven network BSSIDs sent as hunting
    targets. max 15 per payload. s3rloin reports matches.

    TIME SYNC: s3rloin has RTC, Porkchop doesn't.
    CMD_TIME_SYNC with RTT calculation for accuracy.


----[ 6.2 - THE DIALOGUE

    PigSync has a conversation system. three dialogue tracks
    per session. the family has... opinions about your
    capture count.

    Papa greets. Son replies. the tone depends on what
    you're bringing home. empty-handed operators receive
    a different reception than loaded ones. the family
    has a layered emotional vocabulary. each layer has teeth.

    Son has his own opinions. he's... direct.
    the phone has opinions too. the phone judges
    harder than either of them. the phone has seen
    things. the phone remembers. bring captures.
    empty-handed operators get the reception they deserve.

    there are Dark Souls references in the sync hints.
    because of course there are.

    we're not quoting the dialogue here.
    sync and find out. the family dynamics deserve to
    be experienced firsthand, not read in a README.
    (or read the source. pigsync_protocol.h. the pig
     can't stop you. the pig can only judge you.)


----[ 6.3 - BEACON GRUNTS (Phase 3)

    s3rloin broadcasts grunt beacon packets when idle:
    MAC, capture count, battery, storage, mood tier,
    RTC time, uptime, short name.

    connectionless passive awareness. Porkchop can see
    s3rloin's status without initiating a call.

    the son is out there. broadcasting into the void.
    porkchop listens. porkchop waits. porkchop wonders
    if the kid is eating enough captures.

----[ 12.1 - COMMON ISSUES

    "pig won't boot"
        -> reflash firmware via M5 Launcher
        -> try a different USB cable (the cable is guilty until proven innocent)
        -> check power source (USB hub? try direct port. hubs lie.)
        -> 3 rapid reboots = boot guard forces IDLE mode

    "XP gone after reflash"
        -> M5Burner nukes NVS. that's where XP lives.
        -> if you had SD card: XP restores from backup on boot
        -> if you didn't: BACON N00B. our condolences.
        -> use M5 Launcher next time. it preserves NVS.

    "WiFi won't connect in File Transfer"
        -> check SSID/password in settings
        -> 2.4GHz only. 5GHz not supported. the pig is old school.
        -> mDNS: porkchop.local (give it 5-10 seconds)

    "GPS won't lock"
        -> GPS needs sky view. go outside.
        -> check GPS source setting (Grove vs CapLoRa)
        -> default baud: 115200 (configurable in settings)

    "uploads fail / Not Enough Heap"
        -> TLS needs ~35KB contiguous
        -> exit OINK/DNH first (stop promiscuous mode)
        -> check DIAGNOSTICS for heap status
        -> reboot clears fragmentation

    "pig looks sad"
        -> feed it captures
        -> take it for a wardrive
        -> have you considered that the pig might be right?
           malloc(hope): returns valid pointer. sometimes.

----[ 1.4 - ARCHITECTURE (for the silicon gourmets)

    THE CORE:
    cooperative main loop. porkchop.update() (SFX ticks inside),
    Display::update(), Mood::update(). the pig's vital organs.
    single PorkchopMode enum, 24 states. one mode lives. the others wait.
    the pig is a finite state machine with infinite opinions.
    the horse is a barn with load-bearing feelings.

    THE MEMORY WAR:
    no PSRAM means ~300KB internal SRAM for everything.
    TLS needs ~35KB contiguous (kMinContigForTls in heap_policy.h).
    WiFi driver init needs ~70KB (why preInitWiFiDriverEarly() exists).
    the heap fragments like your relationship with sleep.

    HEAP CONDITIONING:
    boot runs a 5-phase ritual: frag blocks (50x1KB), struct blocks
    (20x3KB), TLS test allocs (26KB, 32KB, 40KB). exploits ESP-IDF's
    TLSF allocator for O(1) coalescing. the result: a clean brain
    for TLS handshakes. percussive maintenance for memory.
    the horse calls this "barn defragmentation."
    the barn denies having a defragmentation problem.
    the barn is the horse. denial is structural.

    HEAP MONITORING:
    heap_health.h samples every 1s. auto-triggers conditioning when
    health drops below 65%, clears when it recovers above 75%.
    adaptive cooldown: 15-60s between rounds (scales with heap state).
    the heart bar at the bottom of the screen is heap health.
    100% = clean. 0% = swiss cheese. the pig's blood pressure, basically.

    THE EVENT BUS:
    max 32 queued events, 16 processed per update tick.
    MODE_CHANGE, ML_RESULT, GPS_FIX, GPS_LOST,
    HANDSHAKE_CAPTURED, NETWORK_FOUND, DEAUTH_SENT,
    ROGUE_AP_DETECTED, OTA_AVAILABLE, LOW_BATTERY.
    the pig processes feelings through a state machine.
    the horse processes feelings through a k-hole.

    DUAL-CORE PATTERN:
    WiFi promiscuous callbacks run on core 1 (WiFi task).
    they CANNOT allocate memory or call Serial. instead:
    callback sets volatile flags + writes to static pools.
    main loop on core 0 checks flags and processes safely.
    this is the deferred event pattern. it keeps the WDT happy.
    WDT = Watchdog Timer. also What Did (The pig) Think.

    STATIC POOLS:
    OINK pre-allocates PendingHandshakeFrame pendingHsPool[4]
    (~13KB in BSS). permanent. std::atomic indices for lock-free
    producer/consumer between WiFi task and main loop.
    the pig pays rent on memory it might never use.

    NetworkRecon:
    shared background scanning service. OINK, DONOHAM, SPECTRUM,
    and WARHOG all consume the same getNetworks() vector.
    spinlock mutex with RAII CriticalSection wrapper.
    channel hop order: 1, 6, 11, then 2-5, 7-10, 12-13.
    max 200 networks tracked. the pig has limits.
    (200 is generous. the heap disagrees.)

    JANUS HOG (ESP32-C5 COPROCESSOR):
    the pig grew a second ear. the 5GHz one.
    M5MonsterC5 board connected via Grove UART (115200 8N1).
    runs JanOS/projectZero firmware. speaks scan, attack, monitor.
    peripheral service like GPS -- runs every loop iteration,
    zero heap allocations, all static BSS (~7KB total).
    double-buffered scan cache (64 entries x2) prevents UI flicker.
    5GHz networks injected into NetworkRecon transparently.
    modes don't care WHERE the data came from. they just eat.
    GPS forwarding from C5's onboard AT6668 when local GPS sleeps.
    handshake file import via base64 framed transfer with CRC32.
    the pig doesn't scan 5GHz. the pig DELEGATES 5GHz.
    management is a skill. the pig has management skills now.
    the horse would delegate too but the barn has no peripherals.

    BOOT GUARD:
    RTC memory tracks rapid reboots. 3 in 60 seconds = force IDLE.
    crash loops get the nuclear option. the pig learns from pain.
    the horse calls this progress.

----[ 3.4 - PIG HEALTH (HEAP BAR)

--[ 6 - PIGSYNC (son of a pig)

    ESP-NOW encrypted sync between POPS (Porkchop) and
    SON (s3rloin). the prodigal son answers the phone.


----[ 6.1 - THE PROTOCOL

    press [2] from IDLE to enter PigSync.

    DISCOVERY: broadcast on channel 1. s3rloin responds
    with MAC, pending capture count, flags, RSSI.

    CONNECTION: CMD_HELLO -> RSP_HELLO (session token +
    data channel assignment). channels 3/4/8/9/13 selected
    to avoid congested 1/6/11.

    DATA TRANSFER: chunked, 238 bytes per fragment.
    sequence numbers, CRC32 verification, ACK per chunk.
    5 retries per chunk. 60 second transfer timeout.

    ENCRYPTION: ESP-NOW encrypted unicast.
    PMK and LMK are hardcoded in pigsync_protocol.h.
    (both sides must match. source is truth.
     yes, the keys are pig-themed. obviously.)

    BOUNTIES: wardriven network BSSIDs sent as hunting
    targets. max 15 per payload. s3rloin reports matches.

    TIME SYNC: s3rloin has RTC, Porkchop doesn't.
    CMD_TIME_SYNC with RTT calculation for accuracy.


----[ 6.2 - THE DIALOGUE

    PigSync has a conversation system. three dialogue tracks
    per session. the family has... opinions about your
    capture count.

    Papa greets. Son replies. the tone depends on what
    you're bringing home. empty-handed operators receive
    a different reception than loaded ones. the family
    has a layered emotional vocabulary. each layer has teeth.

    Son has his own opinions. he's... direct.
    the phone has opinions too. the phone judges
    harder than either of them. the phone has seen
    things. the phone remembers. bring captures.
    empty-handed operators get the reception they deserve.

    there are Dark Souls references in the sync hints.
    because of course there are.

    we're not quoting the dialogue here.
    sync and find out. the family dynamics deserve to
    be experienced firsthand, not read in a README.
    (or read the source. pigsync_protocol.h. the pig
     can't stop you. the pig can only judge you.)


----[ 6.3 - BEACON GRUNTS (Phase 3)

    s3rloin broadcasts grunt beacon packets when idle:
    MAC, capture count, battery, storage, mood tier,
    RTC time, uptime, short name.

    connectionless passive awareness. Porkchop can see
    s3rloin's status without initiating a call.

    the son is out there. broadcasting into the void.
    porkchop listens. porkchop waits. porkchop wonders
    if the kid is eating enough captures.

name: PORTAL.HACK DEMO M5STICKC PLUS
description:
### PORTAL.HACK DEMO Firmware

#### Introduction
This demo version of the PORTAL.HACK firmware is designed for security demonstrations and experimental testing. It includes a limited selection of advanced features, such as a depowered RF jammer, the Windows BLE Bad-USB attack, and various test WiFi and BLE functions. This firmware is developed for use with the M5StickC Plus and M5StickC Plus 2 devices, leveraging the capabilities of the ESP32 microcontroller through the Arduino IDE.

#### Included Features

1. **RF Jammer (Depowered)**
   - **Description**: Temporarily disrupts nearby radio signals in a controlled and limited manner.
   - **Usage**: Ideal for testing the effectiveness of RF security countermeasures in controlled environments without causing extensive interference.
   - **Hardware**: Requires the MX-RM-5V receiver module connected to pin 25 and the FS1000A transmitter module connected to pin 26.

2. **Windows BLE Bad-USB**
   - **Description**: Utilizes the M5StickC device to execute "BadUSB" attacks via Bluetooth.
   - **Usage**: The device creates a Wi-Fi network that you can connect to, then access the link http://172.0.0.1/ to input commands, which will be executed when the M5StickC is connected to a Windows PC via USB.

3. **WiFi and BLE Test Functions**
   - **WiFi Scan**: Scans for nearby WiFi networks and displays details such as SSID, signal strength, and security protocols.
   - **BLE Scan**: Scans for nearby Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) devices, showing available devices and their characteristics.

#### Note
This firmware is intended for professional, educational, and demonstration purposes only. Unauthorized use of these features can violate laws and regulations. Always use responsibly and ethically.

name: Palnagotchi for M5 Atom S3(R) Dev Kit
description:
A friendly unit for those lonely Pwnagotchis out there. It's written to run on the M5 Atom S3(R) Dev Kit.

This is a fork of viniciusbo's Palnagotchi for the M5 Cardputer.

He reverse engineered the Pwngrid advertisement protocol and made it possible for the Cardputer to advertise to the Pwngrid as a Pwnagotchi. All brain policy parameters that could negatively impact AI learning were removed from the advertisemenet data.

The Pwngrid works by sending Wifi beacon frames with a JSON serialized payload in Wifi AC headers, containing the Pwnagotchi's data (name, face, pwns, brain policy between others). That's how nearby Pwnagotchis can detect and also learn each other. By crafting a custom beacon frame, this app can appear as a Pwnagotchi to other Pwnagotchis.

name: Paper S3 epub reader with usb disk mode
description:
EPUB e-book reader for M5Stack Paper S3.
Reads .epub files from the SD card.
Supports bookmarks, table of contents, adjustable font size,
and page progress.

Includes extended Latin characters (Czech, Slovak, Polish,
etc.).
Upload books via built-in USB disk mode.

Usage:
- Place .epub files in /books/ folder on the SD card.
- Group multi-volume series into subfolders of /books/
  (for example /books/Dune/). Subfolders are shown in
  the library as collections; tap to open, then tap
  "Back to library" to return to the root list.
- Tap a book title to open it.
- Swipe left/right to turn pages.
- Swipe up to open the menu (both in library and while
  reading). Works even when the SD card has no books —
  you can always reach Settings.
- Use Prev/Next buttons to browse pages when there are
  more books than fit on screen.
- Tap page number in status bar to go to a specific page.
- Tap bookmark icon in status bar to toggle a bookmark.

Library menu:
- Power off
- USB disk mode
- Settings
- Clear cover cache
- Clock

Reader menu:
- Font size (7 levels)
- Display refresh mode (Balanced / Fast / Quality)
- Images on/off (supports progressive JPEG; oversized
  images show a placeholder)
- Chapters (with bookmarks)
- Search
- Go to furthest read position
- Back to library
- Power off

Settings:
- Dark mode — inverted display (white text on black
  background) for comfortable night reading.
- Cover on power off — shows the book cover on the e-ink
  display when powering off.
- Hourly battery refresh — wakes the device every hour
  while powered off to redraw the lock screen with an
  updated battery %. Off by default; shortens battery
  runtime. A user alarm always takes priority.
- Auto power off — automatic shutdown after inactivity
  (off, 5–30 minutes).
- Flip display 180° — manual portrait orientation flip.
- Auto-rotation — IMU-based automatic orientation detection.
- Sync clock (NTP) — connect to WiFi to sync time.
- Alarm — set an alarm that wakes the device from sleep.

Search:
- Full-text search with on-screen keyboard.
- Diacritic-insensitive (matches č as c, etc.).
- Tap a result to jump to it with highlight.
- Navigate between results with Prev/Next bar.

USB disk mode:
- Connect to PC via USB-C.
- The SD card appears as a flash drive.
- Tap screen or eject on PC to exit and reboot.

Footnotes:
- Footnote markers are displayed inline as superscript
  numbers.
- Tap a marker to show the footnote text in a popup.
- Tap anywhere to dismiss.

Clock:
- Large clock display with current time, date, UTC offset,
  last NTP sync time, and alarm status.
- Tap anywhere to return to library.

Alarm:
- Set hour and minute (24-hour format).
- Wakes the device from deep sleep at the scheduled time.
- Beeps periodically until dismissed or auto-dismissed
  after 2 minutes.

玩法：从一间黑屋、一堆将熄的火开始——添柴、生火、吸引流浪者、建造小屋、分配工人、经营贸易站，看着村落在灰白的屏幕上慢慢生长。造出罗盘后踏上「漫漫尘途」：整备背包，走进 61×61 格的程序生成荒原——探索地标、遭遇战斗、攻克矿山，活着回村把战利品和地图落袋；

📦 移植进度：当前版本 v0.10.1，Phase 1 + Phase 2 内容完整（生火间 / 村落 / 贸易站 / 随机事件 / 漫漫尘途 / 荒芜世界 / 战斗 / 14 类地标，含完整地穴地牢与矿山经济闭环）。Phase 3（坠毁星舰）已在规划，后续版本通过本页更新推送。

name: PaperKlipp
description:
PaperKlipp is a lightweight touch UI for M5Stack Paper S3 that connects to a Klipper/Moonraker server over Wi-Fi. It shows live printer status (file name, state, progress, temps, fans, coordinates, print time/ETA/total) and provides touchscreen controls for common actions: preheat presets for bed/nozzle, homing, heaters off, movement/extrusion with selectable step size, toggles (light, filament sensor), and basic job control (start file, pause/resume, cancel with confirmation).

On first boot it runs a setup wizard that scans nearby Wi-Fi networks, lets you enter the password and Klipper host:port (plus optional API key) using an on-screen keyboard, and stores everything locally in flash (no SD card needed). It also includes reconnect/setup buttons and visual press feedback optimized for e-ink.

name: PaperOS v1.2 - Cardputer OS
description:
PaperOS v1.2 — A standalone operating system engineered specifically for the M5Stack Cardputer.

PaperOS turns your Cardputer into a compact workstation and retro-gaming suite, featuring a custom windowless launcher, a full-featured Lua 5.4 environment, and an ecosystem of native applications.

Key Features:
- System & Tools: File Manager with image viewing (pan/zoom/rotate), Paint, 3D Mesh Editor (.obj), Notes, Calculator, Clock, and Piano.
- Connectivity & Web: Lightweight text browser and built-in App Store to fetch Lua apps directly from GitHub over Wi-Fi.
- Media & Audio: Folder-agnostic Music Player with WAV and MP3 playback across the entire SD card.
- Emulation & AI: Hardware-accelerated NES/GB/GBC and Arduboy game emulation, alongside an on-device offline LLM (myAI).
- Developer Environment: Integrated Lua 5.4 console exposing direct hardware controls (GPIO, I2C, Canvas Drawing, Sound, and Timers).

What's New in v1.2:
- Music Player refactor with universal SD folder navigation.
- Automatic Wi-Fi network scanner in Settings.
- Updated Lua runtime memory management and stability fixes.

Requirements:
A FAT32-formatted SD card is required on first boot. Additional assets (PaperEMU.extension for emulation and model.bin for AI chat) as well as full API documentation are available at github.com/Artem76228/PaperOS.

name: Periscope OS: Wifi Attacker Radar
description:
## Tactical Manual: M5StickS3 Wireless Reconnaissance & Spectrum Analyzer Firmware

This updated firmware elevates the M5StickS3 into a unified, passive 
**Electronic Intelligence (ELINT) Station and Live RF Spectrum Visualizer**. Operating entirely passively without transmitting a single RF signal, the device monitors local 2.4 GHz airspace, providing immediate visual feedback on spectrum utilization while tracking, identifying, and logging wireless threats (Deauthentication and Disassociation frames).

---

## Technical Description

The architecture is divided into four highly synchronized core subsystems that manage real-time radio telemetry, digital signal processing, spatial orientation, and data logging.

### 1. Broad-Spectrum RF Visualizer & DPI Sniffer Engine

The single-core 2.4 GHz radio driver is configured for **Promiscuous Mode**, bypassing hardware MAC filters to ingest the raw environment. The sniffer callback handles a dual-pipeline workload:


* **The Spectrum Pipeline:** Unlike previous builds, the radio ingests *every single ambient packet* (Data, Control, and Management frames). Each packet strike exponentially drives the amplitude of the corresponding channel bar on the dashboard.

* **The Deep Packet Inspection (DPI) Pipeline:** The engine simultaneously filters for malicious management frames (Types `0xC0` and `0xA0`). Upon discovery, it performs real-time disassembly to extract the Attacker's MAC, Victim Client MAC, Access Point BSSID, and the 802.11 Disconnection Reason Code.

* **OUI Vendor Profiling:** The first three bytes of a flagged attacker MAC are parsed through an expanded internal lookup table to automatically identify offensive hardware categories (*Espressif/Flipper Zero devices, Raspberry Pi nodes, Alfa long-range cards, Hak5 gear, or Realtek rigs*).

### 2. Live Instrument Dashboard (Landscape Split-Screen)

The UI leverages a landscape layout ($240 \times 135$ pixels) to construct a high-fidelity tactical dashboard divided down the center by a structural pixel boundary.

* **Left Half (Spatial Sonar Disk):** Houses the retro-phosphor circular radar sweep. The sweeping beam simulates a classic CRT display with a 5-layer ghosting decay trail. Active threat sources are plotted as intense glowing blips (a white hot core surrounded by a blood-red aura bloom) that dynamically scale their distance from the crosshairs based on signal strength.

* **Right Half (Equalizer Spectrum Analyzer):** Replaces the historical waterfall with a live **volumetric frequency distribution graph** across Channels 1–11.

* **Peak-Hold Physics:** Floating above each channel bar is a single-pixel **Peak RSSI Tick Line**. When a burst of energy occurs, the tick snaps to the absolute signal power level ($\text{dBm}$) and decays slowly over time, capturing the physical proximity of intermittent or hidden transmitters.

* **Phosphor Dots:** Sitting directly above the spectrum box are 11 micro-indicator pixels. The dot corresponding to the radio core's active channel lights up bright green, providing a minimalist view of the channel hopper's location.

* **Reactor Core Battery Gauge:** Taps into the AXP2101 power management chip, rendering battery life as a vertical analog reactor core rod on the far right edge of the screen.

### 3. Spatial Inertial Processor (Body Shielding Math)

Because omnidirectional antennas lack directional intelligence, the firmware implements an internal calculus integration loop to execute **RF Body Shielding** tracking.

* **Angular Velocity Integration:** The code sample updates the 6-axis IMU (BMI270) to poll raw horizontal rotation velocity from the Z-axis gyroscope (`data.gyro.z`). It computes change-in-time ($dt$) and integrates it to calculate your precise physical heading relative to your boots.

* **Vector Locking:** When your body acts as a physical barrier dampening radio waves behind you, the code continuously compares incoming threat power levels. It binds the strongest peak RSSI value with your physical yaw heading, locking that coordinate line as the primary threat vector on the display.

### 4. Operational Modalities & The Captain's Logbook

* **Target Lock Mode (Button B Click):** Isolates a specific attacker's MAC address profile. The sniffer instantly discards all ambient network chatter to track that single signature across frequencies. The UI drops its green theme for an active tactical cyan layout and frames the target blip inside an automatic rectangular locking reticle.

* **Silent Running Mode (Button A Hold):** Deactivates the display backlights and mutes the speaker completely. Telemetry translates entirely to the internal haptic motor (`GPIO 44`). The motor generates clean haptic pulses that vibrate faster as your body rotates directly into the threat vector line.

* **Proximity Perimeter Breach:** If an active target breaches a critical proximity threshold ($\ge -42\text{ dBm}$), a master priority flag overrides standard operations. The screen flashes blood-red, the haptic motor holds a continuous hum, and the speaker blasts a dual-frequency acoustic naval klaxon horn.

* **The Captain's Log (SPIFFS Database):** Discovered threat metrics are compressed into single, pipe-delimited (`|`) strings and saved to the internal flash filesystem. The Logbook screen parses these data fields to compile standalone, scrollable interactive intelligence sheets.

---

## Directions for Field Operation

### UI Navigation Map & Button Layout

```
             ┌────────────────────────────────┐
             │       [LANDSCAPE MODE]         │
             │                                │
    [B] ─────┤  [RADAR DISK]   │ [SPECTRUM]   │ ◄─── [A] (Main Face Button)
 (Side Button) │   (TRACKER)     │ [HUD DATA]   │
             │                                │
             └────────────────────────────────┘

```

#### 1. Home Radar View

* **Button A - Single Click:** Toggles **Channel Lock**. Instantly freezes the background hopper on the active frequency. Use this the moment you see an active spike on the spectrum visualizer to park the radio core on that frequency.

* **Button A - Press & Hold:** Toggles **Silent Running**. Instantly blacks out the screen and silences audio for haptic-only tracking.

* **Button B - Single Click:** Toggles **Target Lock**. If a threat is actively attacking nearby, clicking this captures its MAC, drops a target box around the blip, and screens out all other wireless activity.

* **Button B - Press & Hold:** Leaves active tracking and drops down into the **Captain's Logbook Deck**.

#### 2. Captain's Logbook View

* **Button A - Single Click:** Cycles forward through saved threat sheets (`SHEET 01/12`, `SHEET 02/12`, etc.) to view individual target assets.

* **Button A - Press & Hold:** Permanently purges and deletes the log registry database from the flash storage.

* **Button B - Press & Hold:** Exits the log deck and re-engages active sonar navigation sweeps.

---

### Executing a Tactical Spectrum Sweep & Fox-Hunt

1. **Broad Airspace Assessment:** Power on the unit. Watch the right-side instrument panel. The vertical bars will bounce dynamically to show ambient traffic density on each channel, while the peak tick lines will register the relative proximity of local routers and client devices.

2. **Threat Acquisition:** If an offensive tool begins executing an injection attack nearby, the outer screen boundaries will flash red, a glowing threat blip will map to the left radar grid, and the speaker will begin chirping.

3. **Locking the Signature:** Note the active channel frequency where the equalizer bar is spiking into the red zone. Click **Button A** to lock your channel hopper to that frequency, then click **Button B** to lock the radar tracking core onto that specific attacker's MAC address profile.

4. **The 360-Degree Sweep:** Hold the M5StickS3 tight and flat against your solar plexus. Rotate your body slowly in a complete circle.

5. **Vector Localization:** When your back is turned to the adversary, your chest blocks the signals; the sonar chirps will slow down to a crawl and the blip will drift away. As you turn and face directly toward the physical location of the threat, the signal passes unhindered. The real-time spectrum bar will maximize, the peak tick will lock to the roof of the grid, the radar blip will snap close to the center crosshairs, and the audio chirps will escalate into a rapid-fire continuous tone.

6. **Closing Distance:** Move forward along that straight-line path vector. If the on-screen telemetry flips to `VCTR: CLOSING` and the pitch rises, you are closing the physical gap to the transmitter. If the device triggers a flashing **BREACH PERIMETER** klaxon blast, the asset machine is in your immediate physical room.

name: Picoware
description:
Open-source custom firmware for PicoCalc, Cardputer ADV, Video Game Module, and other ESP32/Raspberry Pi Pico devices

If installation fails do this instead:
1. Type in `M5Launcher` in the search bar above, then click `Download` next to the M5Launcher firmware.
2. Turn off your Cardputer, then hold the `Go` button on your Cardputer while connecting it to your computer using a USB-C cable until your computer recognizes a new storage device.
3. In M5Burner, click `Burn`, then `Continue`, then change the `COM Port` to the one that corresponds to your Cardputer, and click `Start`.
4. Wait until the flashing process is complete, then disconnect your Cardputer from your computer and turn it on. M5Launcher should now be installed and ready to use!
5. Download the `Picoware-Cardputer.bin` file from the `builds/MicroPython` directory of this repository and copy it to the root of your SD card.
6. With your Cardputer off, insert the SD card into your Cardputer, then turn on your device.
7. Once the app is open, click `SD` then scroll down and select the `Picoware-Cardputer.bin` file, then click `Install`. 
8. Wait until the installation process is complete and your Cardputer will reboot into Picoware!

🚀 Pocket Gambler OS – v1.0.0 (The Final Release)
We made it to 1.0! What started as a simple collection of minigames has evolved into a complete, standalone, handheld operating system for the M5Cardputer. Version 1.0.0 represents the ultimate, stable, and feature-complete vision of the Pocket Gambler OS.

It is a living, breathing digital underworld in your pocket—featuring real-time Wi-Fi crypto trading, RPG progression, dynamic random events, and bulletproof hardware optimization.

🔥 The Complete Feature Set
Live Crypto Terminal: Connect to local Wi-Fi and pull live Bitcoin market data directly from the Binance API. Speculate, buy, sell, and track your P/L (Profit/Loss) in real-time.

The Living OS (Dynamic Events): The system never sleeps. An active background timer generates random events while you navigate the OS. You might get mugged, face a police raid, find a wallet, or suffer a crypto market crash.

The Black Market: An exclusive underground shop (accessible only with $15,000+). Buy permanent perks like VIP Cards (XP multipliers), Bribe Cops, or Tax Evaders to bend the rules of the OS in your favor.

Hardcore Vault Heist: Take out a loan at the Mafia Bank, or risk it all by hacking their vault. Decipher a 6-letter Fallout-style terminal password in just 3 attempts. Win big, or lose half your net worth.

Classic Casino & Slots: Spin the brand-new 3-reel visual Slot Machine, or test your luck in the core games that started it all.

RPG Progression & Analytics: Every dollar won or lost generates XP. Level up your Player Card and watch your wealth grow (or crash) on a dynamic, real-time 50-point vector line graph.

Dynamic Visual Themes: Press t in your Player Card to seamlessly switch the entire OS aesthetic between Neon Cyberpunk, Matrix Hacker, and Blood Casino.

🛡️ v1.0.0 Ultimate Stability & Polish
Bulletproof Hardware Controls: Completely rewrote the input matrix. The OS now reads direct hardware states, mapping standard navigation to the Cardputer's D-pad (. and ;).

The G0 Override: To combat hardware quirks with the Enter key, the silver G0 button (BtnA) on the side of the Cardputer has been hardcoded as a universal, fail-safe ENTER key across the entire OS.

Real-Time OS Kernel: Shifted all internal game loops and random event triggers from frame-based counters to true hardware millis() timers. This completely eliminates UI freezes and soft-locks.

Zero-Crash Architecture: All applications have been packaged into a monolithic, header-only structure, completely bypassing PlatformIO linker errors (vtable crashes) and ensuring flawless compilation.

Atomic Memory Protection: The SD card save.txt structure now safely handles 15 Black Market perks, 50 history nodes, and debt structures, saving atomically after every single transaction to prevent data corruption.

💖 Thank You
Thank you to everyone who followed the development of this project. Grab your M5Cardputer, flash the firmware, and try not to go bankrupt!

The "Crypto Terminal", "Black Market", and all betting modules connect to public APIs purely for entertainment and simulation purposes. No real money, real cryptocurrency, or real financial transactions are executed, stored, or processed by this software. The developer assumes zero responsibility or liability for any financial losses, hardware damage, network security issues, connectivity failures, or data corruption that may occur while using this software. Use at your own risk.

description: The program is composed of M5 BASIC host and Module LoRa (433MHz), which realizes the basic functions of the LoRaWAN470 gateway (single channel and sf). Buy me a coffee--- Ko-fi.com/jonathan2026

Get a Gemini API Key (Free)

1. Go to: https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey
2. Sign in with your Google account.
3. Click “Create API Key” → copy the key (it looks like AIzaSy...).


First Boot Setup
When it boots for the first time:

1. You’ll see the R2-D2 boot screen with countdown and beeps.
Then “Connecting to WiFi...” and “join 'Cardputer-Setup'”.
On your phone:
2. Connect to the WiFi network named Cardputer-Setup.
3. Open a browser and go to 192.168.4.1.
4. Select your home WiFi and enter its password.
In the “Gemini API Key” field, paste your API key from above. 
5. Click Save.

The Cardputer will restart and connect to your WiFi.

You're Ready!
After restart:

You’ll see R2-D2 and “Ready for your next question!”
Type using the keyboard.
Press BtnA (the top button) or Fn + Space to send.
Watch the animated progress bar and hear thinking beeps.
Read R2-D2’s response (scroll with Fn+; / Fn+. if long).
Ask follow-up questions — it remembers the whole conversation!

That’s it! You now have a portable, talking R2-D2 powered by Google Gemini AI.
Enjoy, and may the Force be with you! Beep boop boop! 🤖✨

Functions:

RF433 Reading:

Select this option to read RF433MHz signals.
The device will display "Reading..." and wait for a signal.

If a valid frequency is available, it will emit a signal at that frequency.

Use button B to cycle through these options.

name: RHesus RAdio  (webradio)
description:
Streams ICEcast MP3 and AAC internet radio over Wi-Fi with real-time audio visualizations.  
Stations load from a `station_list.txt` file on the SD card, with built-in defaults if none is found.

---

## Controls

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `BTN A` × 1 | Next station |
| `BTN A` × 2 | Previous station |
| `BTN A` hold | Volume up |
| `/` | Next station |
| `,` | Previous station |
| `;` | Volume up |
| `.` | Volume down |
| `M` | Mute / unmute |
| `S` | Screen on / off (press to sleep, any key to wake) |
| `F` | Fullscreen toggle (hides header) |
| `V` | Cycle visual modes |
| `0–9` | Jump directly to stations 1–10 |

---

## Visual Modes

Cycle through with `V`:

- **Bars** — FFT frequency bars with peak hold
- **Spectrum** — scrolling waveform
- **Both** — bars + waveform combined
- **Liss-Trail** — Lissajous with phosphor trail fade
- **Liss-Line** — Lissajous continuous line
- **Liss-3D** — rotating 3D Lissajous with depth shading
- **VectorScope** — M/S stereo vector scope with phosphor persistence

All modes include a stereo VU meter and volume bar in the header.

---

## Station List

Create a plain text file at the **root of your SD card** named `station_list.txt`.  
One station per line, format: `Name, URL`  
Lines starting with `#` are treated as comments and ignored.

```
# My stations
Radio Tango, http://ais-edge148-pit01.cdnstream.com/2202_128.mp3
Radio Soyuz, http://65.109.84.248:8100/soyuzfm-192.mp3
My AAC Station, http://example.com/stream.aacp
```

- Supports up to **100 stations**
- MP3 and AAC / AAC+ streams supported
- If no SD card or file is found, 4 built-in default stations are used
- Last played station and volume are saved and restored on boot

---

## Notes

- Streams over HTTP only (HTTPS is not supported by the ICY stream library)
- 1 MB stream buffer (~40 s at 192 kbps) for smooth playback
- Audio decode task runs on PRO_CPU at priority 2 for stable performance
- Wi-Fi credentials configured via `CardWifiSetup`

It features a simulated boot sequence with modem handshake, RTC, sleep/doze function, secrets, compass, instrument panel, system messages, secrets, ambient noises while awake, time display with face-melting retro phosphor burn, glorious new audio, settings menu, WY-DCM/Xenoflux, badge collection system, user tracking and intermode behavioral feedback, some secret stuff, mail (infinite and forever) secrets, sound test, and some lore. It's a whole experience, and takes a little time to tease out all the features. You'll get occasional mail related to settings and modes you explore, and probably unlock some things. Fun things, mostly. 
***NOW FEATURING BAD BUG***
Play BAD BUG right from the WY submenu, no unlock required!
Eat your prey! Hear them SCREAM! BATHE IN BLOOD! Gain eggs to lay (press A) when faced with a marine! Map in the HUD tracks your whereabouts and facility status! Clear all 16 rooms to trigger FACILITY CLEARED and enter the vent. (VENTCRAWL coming soon!)

WY-DCM, known to the end-user as Xenoflux, is a plasma-routing simulator designed by the company to harvest spare cog-cycles and reclaim contracted downtime. In exchange for solving distributed genetic sequencing problems, the company grants the end-user bonus credits. Building better genetic code. For profit! Xenoflux is a FUN GAME that does not track ANY USER BIOLOGICAL DATA, EVER. Performance metrics, on the other hand...


Explore, have fun, and embrace the glitches. Mostly they're intentional lore. Mostly.
Navigation from Watch screen:
hold buttonA = enter settings
press buttonB = enter instrument panel/return to watch



A fun project for the m5stickcplus2, untested on any other hardware.

BETA VERSION, BUGS ARE EXPECTED. Check for updates.

name: RadiacodeCardputer
description:
# RadiacodeCardputer

Turn your M5Cardputer into a pocket radiation dashboard for the RadiaCode-102 detector.

Connect over Bluetooth LE and read live dose rate, accumulated dose, and CPS straight from
your RadiaCode — no phone required. Watch the live energy spectrum, hear every count as a
geiger click, and get a loud two-tone alarm when dose-rate crosses your limit.

Features:
- Live Main / Spectrum / Menu views on the Cardputer screen
- Realtime dose rate, dose, and CPS readings
- Live energy-spectrum graph
- Geiger-click audio + alarms duplicated from the device
- SD-card logging of measurements
- Settings saved locally (NVS + SD); 4 brightness levels
- Auto-reconnect to your RadiaCode

Hardware: M5CardputerADV (ESP32-S3). Pairs with RadiaCode-101/102/103.

recommended update focused on Bub storage/import safety and lifecycle fixes.

This hotfix hardens the Bub storage and import system to prevent active pets from being accidentally overwritten or lost. Stored pet flows are now safer and more consistent, the currently loaded pet is hidden from storage lists, and a new "Store Current Pet" option has been added directly to the storage menu.

v2.2.3
Fixes intermittent title screen background disappearing after provisioning. Improves overall performance and stabilizes mini-game rendering and asset handling.

v2.2.2  Lifecycle Fixes
Fixed ghost pet appearing after setup or burial
Enforced “no save = no pet” across all systems
Disabled pet actions when no pet is loaded
Fixed warwalking rewards triggering without a pet
Stability improvements to background systems and UI
All install paths tested and stable

v2.2.1 (Hotfix on steroids)
Major improvements to boot flow, asset handling, and time system. Manual asset installs now work correctly, and offline setup is fully supported. Fixed issues with incorrect pet age, SD/asset detection, and input blocking on error screens. Console is now accessible even in failure states. Warwalking rewards rebalanced.

Autonomous pet actions
Passive XP gain
Step counter with ambient rewards (War Walking)

Fixes asset provisioning issues that could stall downloads and improves OTA reliability, including recovery from interrupted or unstable connections. Added fallback CDN to improve availability of assets and manifests.  Also refines alert and audio behavior and improves death flow handling.

Timezone auto-detection + expanded support
Auto Clock idle mode

Added a timeout fallback for BOOT_NTP_WAIT

Fixed the manual timezone path so it starts the NTP wait timer correctly
Added support for the Moscow timezone in boot-time timezone detection

This release improves recovery when NTP is unavailable or blocked and prevents users from getting trapped in the boot time-sync flow.

Fixed reprovision loop triggered by rescue flow
Unified WiFi handling for asset provisioning
repair assets now runs without requiring reboot

name: Raspyjack (v1/v1.1/ADV)
description:
Turn your Cardputer into a remote companion for RaspyJack running on a Raspberry Pi.
This is not RaspyJack itself, it connects to your existing RaspyJack setup and lets you control it using the Cardputer screen and keyboard.

Setup & General Controls
-Press any key during boot to open Settings or hold BtnA on top right to get back to settings
-Configure Wi-Fi first, then add your RaspyJack host
-Hold BtnA during a session to return to Settings
-Press BtnA in menus to go back
-Press D to edit Wi-Fi or host profiles
-Press DEL to delete a saved Wi-Fi or host
-Use Factory Reset to erase all saved data

Streaming Controls (RaspyJack)
1 = Key 1
2 = Key 2
3 = Key 3
Arrow keys = Navigate menus
W / A / S / D = Alternative navigation (same as arrows)
Enter = Open menus or launch a payload

Important Note
-Some Wi-Fi payloads may interrupt the stream
-After exiting such payloads, press the reset button on the Cardputer to restart the session
-Not all payloads fully support keyboard input yet
-A dedicated keyboard helper is required and is not yet implemented in all payloads (In Process)
-However, all payloads can still be navigated and controlled using the available controls

Make sure you flash your rpi with the latet Raspyjack version
Raspyjack main project by 7h30th3r0n3:
https://github.com/7h30th3r0n3/Raspyjack

| +/- | 调节参数 |
| W/A/S/D | 视角控制（键盘模式） |
| I | 切换 IMU / 键盘视角 |
| C | 开关对比模式（场景2） |
| E | 切换模式（场景4/5） |
| R | 重置视角 |
| H | 开关 HUD |
| ? | 帮助面板 |

name: SH. speedometer stick-c plus 2
description:
speedometer for a bicycle, motorcycle, etc. based on a Hall sensor

1. Required components:
M5StickC Plus 2: The device itself.
Hall sensor: For example, KY-024 (linear) or KY-003 (digital). For a speedometer, a digital sensor is better, which produces a clear HIGH/LOW signal when a magnet is detected.
Magnet: A neodymium magnet that will be attached to the wheel.
Connecting wires.
Grove cable (optional): If you are using the Grove port of the M5StickC Plus 2.
2. Connecting the Hall sensor:
The M5StickC Plus 2 has several available GPIO. We will use one of them.

VCC (power) of the Hall sensor -> 5V or 3.3V on the M5StickC Plus 2 (check the specification of your sensor).
GND (ground) of the Hall sensor -> GND on the M5StickC Plus 2.
OUT (signal pin) of the Hall sensor -> GPIO 32 on the M5StickC Plus 2. (GPIO 32 is available on the Grove port as SDA, but it can be used as a regular GPIO).

**Important:** Make sure that your Hall sensor produces a signal level compatible with the 3.3V logic of the ESP32. Most digital Hall sensors have a built-in comparator and work with 3.3V. If you have a 5V sensor, you may need a voltage divider on the signal line, but this is usually not necessary as the ESP32 is tolerant of 5V inputs up to a certain threshold.
